activity_context.topic_title: Writing Geometric Series in Sigma Notation

feedback.problem: The first term of a geometric sequence is $-5$ and the common ratio is $6.$ Written in sigma notation, what is the sum of the first $22$ terms?
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we must express the series in the form:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{N}{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1},
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ denotes the first term of the series, $r$ denotes the common ratio, and $N$ denotes the number of terms in the series. In this case, ${a}_{1}=-5,$ $r=6$ and $N=22.$

Expressing the geometric series in sigma notation, we obtain:

$$
{S}_{22}={\sum }_{n=1}^{22}(-5)\cdot {6}^{n-1}\,\,
$$

Finally, we can simplify the above using the laws of exponents, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{22}(-5)\cdot {6}^{n-1} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{22}(-5)\cdot {6}^{n}\cdot {6}^{-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{22}(-5)\cdot {6}^{-1}\cdot {6}^{n} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{22}(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{6}\cdot {6}^{n} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{22}(-\frac{5}{6}){6}^{n}\end{aligned}
$$
